title: Zip Lines and High Ropes in the UK: A Family Guide
description: Zip lines and high ropes for families in the UK: treetop courses, giant zip wires in Wales and the Lake District, age, height and weight rules and what to wear.
h1: Zip lines and high ropes in the UK
intro: Wobbly rope bridges, Tarzan swings and wind-in-your-face zip wires. Here’s how to plan a high-flying family adventure in the UK.
cardText: Treetop courses and giant zip wires, plus the rules to check.

blocks.title: Scout’s high-wire tip
blocks.text: Course rules (age, height, weight and supervision ratios) decide what your family can do together. Check them before you book, not on the day.

sections.html: Treetop adventure courses, such as Go Ape, have rope bridges, ladders and zip wires through the forest, with junior courses for younger children. You’re clipped on throughout, and instructors brief you first.
Zip World runs big zip lines in Wales and the Lake District, alongside underground and trampoline adventures. Bigger rides usually have higher minimum ages and weight limits.

• Under-16s often need a participating adult.
  • Courses can close in high winds or storms.
  • Tell staff about medical conditions.

See all zip lines and adventure parks.

faqs.q: Is there a weight limit for zip lines?
faqs.a: Many zip lines have minimum and maximum weight limits for safety. Check the provider’s rules for each ride.
